format.p1: Parent post. No URL. Stands alone if nobody opens the reply.
format.p2: First reply on that post. Close + dest. This is the straw — same machine as Barakhlo, different voice.

voice: US licensing candidate between shifts. American English. Native Threads: story or pain in p1, concrete numbers + soft CTA in p2. No subscribe, no Gumroad on first touch. Not a brochure. Took/ran the mock — never sat the official paper.

profile.name: UniPrep US
profile.bio: Free timed US mocks. Topic report, no account. SIE, 7, 63, CA real estate, PTCE. Not FINRA or the state board.

rules: American English. US certifications only — no CIPLE, CCSE, Leben in Deutschland, Life in the UK.
Each day is a thread: p1 parent (no URL), p2 first reply (close + dest).
Name the exam body and the mock numbers. If they differ from the official test, say so.
CTA is the free timed mock, not Anki. No signup.
Not official FINRA / NASAA / DRE / PTCB / ServSafe / DMV material.
Topic tag = that exam, not a generic study tag.
State real estate: always name the state. Never 'the real estate exam'.
USCIS civics is oral (10 from 100). Do not treat the 30Q MCQ as the interview.
took / ran / take — not sat / sitting / paper. advisor, not adviser.
Point-edit 2026-09-23: diversify duplicate hooks (≈22 P1s); add hook_type/content_mode/repetition_group/modifier. No bank rewrite, no dest/topic change.

pin.p1:
US licensing mocks. Timed. Topic score when you finish. No account.

SIE, Series 7/63, California DRE, PTCE, ServSafe, CDL. Independent practice — not FINRA, not the state board.

Take the mock first. Anki only for the topics you failed.

days.p1: I thought SIE was a short online quiz. It’s 75 questions on a 105-minute clock with a 70% line — FINRA’s outline length, not a 20-question blog mock.
days.p2: Products and risks are ~44%. I want pass/no-pass plus the weak domain. Independent. Not FINRA.

days.p1: I don’t have 105 minutes before a shift. I needed a shorter SIE screen that still hits the four domains.
days.p2: 25 questions / 35 minutes here — a diagnostic, then the full 75 when I have time. Still not FINRA.

days.p1: Series 7 weekends are long. A 40-question “lite” mock lied about readiness.
days.p2: I run 60Q / 90 min across job functions. Report names what I missed. Independent — check FINRA’s outline.

days.p1: Boss said I needed Series 63. I almost kept studying Series 7. Wrong license.
days.p2: 63 = state securities law (NASAA). This check: 60Q / 75 min / 72% line. Confirm your state. Not Series 7.

days.p1: I bought a “US real estate” pack. California agency and disclosures were three slides with a palm-tree emoji.
days.p2: DRE tests California. This diagnostic is 60Q / 90 min / 70%. Salesperson has national + CA portions. Not DRE.

days.p1: Pharmacy tech job: “PTCE required.” Blog quiz was 15 items. Real shape is ~90 questions and a long clock.
days.p2: I run 90Q / 110 min with a 70% diagnostic line. Medications dominate. Independent — not PTCB. Check ptcb.org.

days.p1: Kitchen said ServSafe Manager card before I could open alone. Facebook quiz was 10 questions. Usual format is 90/120/75.
days.p2: I run that length on a timer with a topic report. Independent — not National Restaurant Association. Confirm your state.

days.p1: CLP written is state DMV off the FMCSA handbook. My “CDL app” had truck memes and zero space-management questions.
days.p2: 60 general-knowledge on a timer: inspection, space, cargo, hours. Not the DMV test. Endorsements are separate.

days.p2: Free timed mocks, no signup. US licensing catalog. Independent — we don’t sell your score to FINRA.

days.p1: PTCE calculation check: quantity 30, take one tablet twice daily. I answered 30 days. It is 15. What step do you write first?
days.p2: Tablets per day first: 1 × 2 = 2. Then 30 ÷ 2 = 15 days. Independent practice — not PTCB.

days.p1: I could score well on short PTCE quizzes. My first full timed run exposed how much slower I was once calculations and drug questions piled up.
days.p2: Run the long clock before trusting the score. Independent practice — not PTCB.

days.p1: Sig check: “ii tabs po bid.” I used to decode each piece and forget the daily total. How many tablets does the patient take per day?
days.p2: Two tablets by mouth twice daily = four tablets per day. Independent practice — not PTCB.

days.p1: Concentration trap: 1:1000 means 1 gram in 1000 mL. I kept missing the next conversion. How many mg are in one mL?
days.p2: 1 gram = 1000 mg, so the concentration is 1 mg/mL. Independent practice — not PTCB.

days.p1: The refrigerator log is outside range. Quietly resetting the thermometer is not a fix. What is your first safe action?
days.p2: Quarantine affected stock and follow the pharmacy’s escalation procedure. Independent practice — not PTCB.

days.p1: Hydralazine and hydroxyzine look close enough to punish fast reading. Which extra detail do you check before selecting the product?
days.p2: Read the full drug name, strength, dosage form, and indication context. Independent practice — not PTCB.
